compiled_state.title: Add context-augmentation loop, prompt caching, and turn-budget exhaustion handling to CI LLM review pipeline
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

CI LLM reviewers in standard, deep, and overlay tiers (running on the Python module + LiteLLM abstraction shipped by epic c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968) receive only the diff. Local `/dso:review` reviewers — running in Claude Code's harness with full tool access — make 20-40 grounded tool calls per review to verify call sites, deletion impact, cross-file consistency, and framework-guarantee defenses against the actual codebase. CI reviewers therefore produce lower-fidelity findings on the same diff: speculation about callers, missed cross-file regressions, and false-positive defenses that a quick file read would refute.

This epic closes the CI <-> local fidelity gap by adding an application-level context-augmentation loop where the model emits structured context-request blocks (action + arguments — e.g., `{"action": "read_files", "paths": [...]}`, `{"action": "grep", "patterns": [...], "paths": [...]}`) as fenced text in plain-text assistant messages; the dispatcher parses any request blocks, executes them locally, and appends the results as a new user message before issuing the next `litellm.completion(...)` call. The provider-native tool-use API (`tools=[...]`, `tool_use` content blocks, `tool_calls` arrays) is deliberately not used — every call's message history is provider-agnostic plain text, which (a) sidesteps LiteLLM's known cross-provider tool-use translation bugs (LiteLLM #18271, #26529) and (b) preserves clean cross-provider fallback as configured by the LiteLLM substrate epic (c6de SC6). Industry pattern survey across multi-provider repo-aware AI tools (aider, Cline, OpenHands, SWE-agent) confirms this is the dominant pattern; PR-Agent demonstrates the single-shot alternative is less fit-for-purpose given the fidelity gap this epic targets. Light tier remains diff-only, single-shot.

Caching and turn-budget exhaustion handling ship together with the loop because they are load-bearing for one another: without prompt caching, the per-turn input-token cost across 15+ tool-style turns is prohibitive (the input prefix is re-sent every turn); without the soft-cap -> second-nudge -> fail-closed cascade, a misbehaving reviewer can loop indefinitely on a confused diff and either burn budget or hang the CI gate. Provider/tier fallback ships at the LiteLLM substrate layer (c6de SC6) — not in this epic — since it is fundamentally a substrate concern.

Outcome: PR authors see CI review comments grounded in actual code references (file:line citations) instead of speculative findings, reducing dismissed-as-noise rate and increasing review-verdict trust parity with local /dso:review.

## Success Criteria

- Application-level context-augmentation loop active for standard, deep (3 specialists + arch synthesis), and overlay reviewers; each can request additional context during its turn by emitting a structured request block in its assistant message per a documented contract (`docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md`). The dispatcher parses request blocks **only from assistant-role messages**, never re-parsing user-role / diff content (defending against the failure mode where a PR diff or a docs change containing literal example request syntax would otherwise be re-interpreted as a request). The dispatcher executes parsed requests locally and appends the results as a new user message before issuing the next `litellm.completion(...)` call. The provider tool-use API is not used — every call's message history is provider-agnostic plain text. Light tier dispatched in single-shot mode (no augmentation loop) and remains diff-only. Parser handles failure modes including the model emitting both a well-formed request block and a final-findings block in the same assistant message: well-formed-request takes precedence and findings are deferred to a subsequent turn. The structured-request format and the request-precedence rule are documented in the contract so request-block parsing is testable independently of the LLM call. Verified by context-request logs in fixture-corpus runs evidencing standard / deep reviewers grounding findings in fetched data (each such finding cites a `file:line` resolved by a recorded request-response cycle), light reviewers producing findings from the diff alone (no requests in the log), and parser unit tests against well-formed and malformed assistant outputs (including outputs that contain literal request-syntax in user-role positions, which must NOT trigger execution).
- `read_files` and `grep` tool implementations enforce a security boundary: repo-root jail (absolute paths and `..` parent traversal rejected; **paths canonicalized via realpath and re-verified to resolve under repo root, defending against committed or runtime-created symlinks pointing to /etc, $HOME, or sibling worktrees**); per-file size cap (configurable; default 256 KB); per-tool-result max output bytes (configurable; default 64 KB) with an explicit truncation marker appended when the cap is hit and an instruction to the model not to assert absence based on truncated content; **per-grep-invocation wall-clock timeout (configurable; default 5s) and binary-file exclusion (or use ripgrep with `--max-filesize`) to prevent ReDoS-class regex patterns from pinning a CI core**. Verified by unit tests covering absolute-path rejection, parent-traversal rejection, **symlink-escape rejection (test fixtures with both committed symlinks and runtime-created symlinks pointing outside repo root)**, file-size-cap rejection, multi-pattern multi-path tool argument acceptance, **grep-timeout enforcement with adversarial regex (e.g., `(a+)+$` against a long line)**, and truncation-marker emission.
- Anthropic prompt caching active with two `cache_control` breakpoints (after the system prompt; after the diff). OpenAI prefix caching applies automatically. The `cache_control` placement is derived from the rendered message structure at call time (not hardcoded by index), defending against agents that inject agent-specific instructions between system and diff. **A prefix-bytes hash invariant test asserts the cached prefix is byte-identical across turns within a run**, defending against silent invalidation from per-turn dynamic content (timestamps, turn counters, agent_id interpolation, randomized tip ordering, trailing whitespace from template rendering). A cache-hit assertion emits a warning to CI logs when `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens > 0` does not occur on the first Anthropic call per review run **AND `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` is also zero** (tolerating the legitimate first-call cache-warm case where a CI job is retried within the 5-minute Anthropic cache TTL); subsequent turns warn when `cache_read_input_tokens` does not increase. Verified by unit test asserting `cache_control` placement at the documented boundaries, prefix-bytes-hash invariant test across turns, and integration test asserting cache-creation on turn 1 and cache-read on turn 2 against a fixture review.
- Soft-cap nudge cascade: a per-tier configurable soft cap (**default 15 turns**) triggers a wrap-up nudge instructing the model to emit final `reviewer-findings` JSON. **If the model continues emitting structured context-request blocks past `soft_cap + 3` turns, a second harder nudge runs.** **Post-nudge state-machine rule: when an assistant turn after the first nudge contains both a well-formed request block and a final-findings block, the request is ignored AND counts as a strike toward the second nudge — preventing infinite loops where deferring findings indefinitely defeats the cap.** If the model still does not emit final JSON after the second nudge, the review records as failed (fail-closed) via the existing `record-review.sh` integration. Verified by tests covering: nudge -> final JSON path; second nudge -> fail-closed recording; per-tier soft-cap override; post-nudge mixed request+findings turn -> request ignored, strike counted.
- Before / after fixture-corpus delta: post-loop CI runs surface a documented number of additional grounded findings (each citing a `file:line` resolved by a context request) compared to the pre-loop baseline captured in story 1 of epic c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968. Comparison runs at epic close as a one-shot script and the delta is reported in the close artifact; per-fixture grounded-finding counts shift from zero (pre) to non-zero (post) on at least 60% of fixtures. **Quality-not-just-presence assertion: on a curated subset (>=5 fixtures) where local /dso:review findings are known, post-change CI findings overlap with local findings on >=N critical/important items (N defined per fixture in the curated set), OR speculation-marker frequency ("likely", "probably", "may break callers") in CI finding text decreases by >=25% relative to the pre-loop baseline.**
- Per-feature unit tests using `respx` / `httpx.MockTransport`-style provider mocks cover: structured-request parsing (well-formed + malformed assistant outputs, including outputs with literal request-syntax in user-role positions), context-request dispatch (single + multiple requests in one assistant turn), soft-cap nudge state machine (each branch of the cascade including post-nudge mixed turn rule), `cache_control` breakpoint placement under all four (tier x tools-present) combinations, prefix-bytes-hash invariant across turns, jail enforcement (including symlink escape rejection and grep-timeout enforcement), and output truncation. Integration tests exercise the loop end-to-end against both Anthropic and OpenAI providers with fixture reviews. (Provider/tier fallback dispatch tests live in c6de's SC6 — out of scope here.)

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Resource: tool-mocking strategy in unit tests
  Interaction: e471-dda3 (Confluence integration / reference-library URL fetching) introduces curl-based fetching; this epic's loop's `read_files` is file-only (must NOT fetch URLs).
  Gate: document `read_files` semantics as filesystem-only; ensure the contract description rules out URL fetching so the model does not attempt a URL argument.
- Resource: reviewer agent system prompts
  Interaction: 4911-c7ba (Reviewer rubric expansion) modifies reviewer prompts; this epic adds context-request availability instructions to reviewer prompts. Different regions of the prompt; both can proceed in parallel if the request-availability prompt section is added before 4911-c7ba's rubric expansion lands.
  Gate: parallel-safe; document context-request availability in the rubric expansion so reviewers know which actions are available per tier.
- Resource: reviewer-findings.json finding shape
  Interaction: 4b8f-924d (Severity-only review schema) removes scores; this epic adds grounded findings that cite `file:line` evidence. Both modify the findings stream but at different layers (schema fields vs. finding-content shape).
  Gate: this epic's grounded-finding format must conform to whichever schema is current at merge time (post-4b8f-924d if it lands first; pre-4b8f-924d otherwise).
- Resource: cross-provider switch wastes Anthropic prompt cache built up earlier in a run
  Interaction: c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968 SC6 (provider/tier fallback) may switch providers mid-run; this epic's SC3 cache effort is wasted on the alternate provider.
  Gate: mitigation deferred to integration time once both epics are merged — candidate mitigations include fallback-after-N-turns demotion to fail-closed, or a per-run cost ceiling (tracked in c6de's cross-epic interactions). If cost cliff is observed in production, a follow-up bug ticket addresses the integration.
- Resource: `docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md` referenced by reviewer agent prompt examples
  Interaction: agent prompts (in `plugins/dso/agents/*.md`) embed examples of the context-request format. Drift between the contract doc and the agent prompts produces parser rejections during partial rollouts.
  Gate: contract carries a `version` field; a referential-integrity check (similar to existing `check-skill-refs.sh`) validates agent prompt examples against the current contract version at pre-commit time.

## Scenario Analysis

- Cross-provider fallback bypasses cache and inflates cost (medium, runtime): when c6de's fallback fires mid-run, the alternate provider sees a cold prefix, wasting the Anthropic prompt cache built across earlier turns. Mitigation: documented in cross-epic interactions; integration-time mitigation deferred (fallback-after-N-turns demotion or per-run cost ceiling); follow-up bug ticket if observed in production.
- Contract doc drift between dispatcher and agent prompts (medium, deployment): `docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md` evolves but agent prompts embed old-format examples. Mitigation: contract version field in request blocks; referential-integrity check on agent prompt examples.
- CI runner filesystem differs from local repo layout (medium, deployment): GitHub Actions checkouts may use shallow clones, sparse checkouts, or symlinked workspace dirs; `read_files` for a file outside the checkout cone returns file-not-found, which the model may interpret as "file deleted" rather than "unavailable in this CI context." Mitigation: explicit fetch-depth / sparse-checkout requirements documented as CI prereqs; tool result for missing files distinguishes "not in checkout" from "does not exist in repo."
- Soft-cap default 15 turns interacts poorly with deep-tier 4 agents (medium, configuration): deep tier dispatches 3 specialists in parallel plus an arch synthesis agent serially; if each consumes ~15 turns, total turns per review is 60+, and Anthropic/OpenAI per-minute token rate limits apply per-key. Parallel deep-tier reviews on a busy repo can self-induce the 429s that trigger c6de SC6 fallback. Mitigation: SC4 per-tier configurable cap allows tightening defaults for deep-tier specialists separately; document the multiplier in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md.
- Per-file 256 KB cap defeats reading generated/lockfile artifacts (medium, configuration): default cap silently truncates package-lock.json, poetry.lock, large test fixture JSON, generated migration files. Truncation marker is per SC2, but the model receiving truncated content may make grounded-looking findings on incomplete data. Mitigation: SC2 truncation marker carries an explicit instruction to the model not to assert absence based on truncated content; consider per-extension caps in a follow-up if observed in production.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968 (Python migration + LiteLLM provider abstraction + provider/tier fallback — this epic operates on the merged dso_ci_review/ module and depends on SC6's `streaming=False` + fallback substrate).

## Research Findings

- Industry pattern survey (multi-provider repo-aware AI tools): aider, Cline, OpenHands (NonNativeToolCallingMixin fallback), SWE-agent (text parsers) dominantly implement application-level loops with text/XML-parsed structured requests rather than provider-native tool-use. Cline (the most-starred agent) uses XML-in-system-prompt despite being Anthropic-first because it works uniformly across providers. Aider explicitly observed that forcing GPT through function-calling degraded coding quality vs. structured-text emission. PR-Agent (Codium/Qodo) — closest to this CI reviewer use case — sidesteps the loop with single-shot diff compression but does not claim equivalent fidelity to a loop-based reviewer. Key insight: confirms the architectural choice. Key gotcha: Cline issue #3992 documents the failure mode where the model emits structured-request syntax as literal text rather than as parseable request — parser fence-strictness and assistant-role-only scanning are mitigations. Sources: aider docs, Cline issue #3992, OpenHands issue #8424, PR-Agent docs.
- LiteLLM tool-use translation bugs: LiteLLM's parallel-tool-result merging on Anthropic has documented production issues (#18271, #26529); related issues #16711 (Claude Code tool result incompatible with LiteLLM), #5277 (Bedrock parallel tool calls), PR #15315 (partial fix for Anthropic passthrough). These bugs only affect provider-native tool-use; this epic's plain-text completion path sidesteps them entirely.
- Anthropic prompt caching: cache prefix order is tools, system, then messages; `cache_control` on the last tool definition caches all tool definitions; up to 4 breakpoints. Two breakpoints (after system, after diff) keep both cached across the multi-turn loop. Source: platform.claude.com/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching.
- OpenAI prefix caching: automatic for prompts >=1024 tokens; no `cache_control` flag needed.

## Approach

Build directly on c6de's merged Python module + LiteLLM abstraction (including SC6 provider/tier fallback): extend `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` with an application-level context-augmentation loop using plain-text `litellm.completion(...)` calls (no provider tool-use API); add `read_files` and `grep` request handlers with a realpath-canonicalized repo-root jail, per-file size caps, grep wall-clock timeout, and per-result truncation; add Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoints (after system, after diff) derived from the rendered message structure with a prefix-bytes-hash invariant test and a cache-hit assertion that tolerates CI-retry cache-warm state; add a soft-cap nudge state machine that emits a wrap-up nudge at turn 15, then a second harder nudge at turn 18, then records the review failed via `record-review.sh`. Light tier dispatched in single-shot mode without the augmentation loop. Provider/tier fallback dispatch is inherited from c6de's substrate work — no fallback logic in this epic.

### Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered
  - Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (LiteLLM tool-use API surface, Anthropic prompt caching with cache_control), novel architectural pattern (multi-turn application-level context-augmentation loop in CI without provider tool-use)
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered
  - Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 7 critical/high folded into SC text directly; 5 medium retained in Scenario Analysis section
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: re-brainstorm to (a) reframe architecture from provider tool-use to custom application-level loop after user clarified the design, (b) migrate provider/tier fallback work to c6de per Scope reviewer recommendation, (c) absorb 7 critical/high Red Team findings into SC text
- Industry pattern survey (Step 2.6 supplement): triggered — aider, Cline, OpenHands, PR-Agent, SWE-agent verified custom-loop dominance for multi-provider repo-aware AI tools
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): VERIFIED for plain-text custom-loop architecture against Anthropic + OpenAI; the prior INSUFFICIENT-EVIDENCE risk for cross-provider tool-use translation does not apply since this epic does not use provider tool-use
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keyword: agent definitions (reviewer agent system prompts gain a context-request availability section as part of this epic)
- Scale context (Step 0): small scale (default — bounded turn count via soft cap; per-review token cost bounded by caching + cap)
